title: Graded cubical partition map and diagonal translation
statement:
Let $r\geq0$, $D=\mathbf Z^r$, and $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ be its ordered standard basis. Let $C_a$ be the free abelian group on $[v,I]$ for $v\in D$ and $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ of cardinality $a$, zero outside $0\leq a\leq r$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Equip it with the differential and augmentation of [lem-sfb-integral-lattice-cubical-contraction], explicitly
$$d[v,I]=\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^{\#\{j\in I:j<i\}}([v+u_i,I\setminus\{i\}]-[v,I\setminus\{i\}]),\quad d|_{C_0}=0,\quad e[v,\varnothing]=1.$$
Put $T_n=\bigoplus_{a+b=n}C_a\otimes_{\mathbf Z}C_b$ and define on homogeneous pure tensors
$$d_T(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^a x\otimes dy\quad(x\in C_a).$$
This formula is well defined, $d_T^2=0$, and $T$ is a chain complex, with the tensor and chain-complex notions of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Let $u_A=\sum_{i\in A}u_i$ and $\epsilon(A,B)=(-1)^{\#\{(a,b)\in A\times B:b<a\}}$. There is a unique family of homomorphisms $P_n:C_n\to T_n$ specified on the free basis by
$$P_{|I|}[v,I]=\sum_{A\sqcup B=I}\epsilon(A,B)[v,A]\otimes[v+u_A,B].$$
For each $I$ the sum has $2^{|I|}$ terms, each in total degree $|I|$. The components $P_n$ are zero whenever $C_n=0$. For every $w\in D$, define $\tau_w[v,I]=[v+w,I]$ and use diagonal translation on $T$. Then
$$P_n\tau_w=(\tau_w\otimes\tau_w)P_n\quad\text{for every integer }n.$$
In particular this is equivariance of a degree-preserving homomorphism of graded abelian groups; it does not assert that $P$ commutes with the differentials.

proof.text: Fix $a,b$ with $a+b=n$. The function $(x,y)\mapsto dx\otimes y+(-1)^a x\otimes dy$ is $\mathbf Z$-bilinear, because $d$ is additive and tensoring is bilinear. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] therefore gives a unique homomorphism $C_a\otimes C_b\to T_{n-1}$, using the summand inclusions of bidegrees $(a-1,b)$ and $(a,b-1)$. Define $d_T$ on a direct-sum element by summing these homomorphisms over its finitely many nonzero components. This is additive, has degree $-1$, and gives precisely the stated formula; terms with a zero factor are zero.

proof.text:
By [lem-sfb-integral-lattice-cubical-contraction], $d^2=0$ on $C$. For $x\in C_a$, $y\in C_b$, expansion of step 1 gives
$$d_T^2(x\otimes y)=d^2x\otimes y+\bigl((-1)^{a-1}+(-1)^a\bigr)dx\otimes dy+(-1)^{2a}x\otimes d^2y=0.$$
The middle coefficients cancel. If $a=0$, the terms involving $dx$ are already zero, so the same calculation applies. The pure tensors generate each summand by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and direct-sum elements have finite support, so $d_T^2=0$ everywhere. This is the chain-complex condition of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology], including zero degrees.

proof.text: The ordered partitions $A\sqcup B=I$ are in bijection with subsets $A\subseteq I$, by $A\mapsto(A,I\setminus A)$. Each of the $|I|$ elements has two choices of part, independently, so there are $2^{|I|}$ terms. Each summand $\epsilon(A,B)[v,A]\otimes[v+u_A,B]$ lies in $C_{|A|}\otimes C_{|B|}\subseteq T_{|I|}$ since $|A|+|B|=|I|$. Thus the displayed finite sum defines an element $p(v,I)\in T_{|I|}$, also for $I=\varnothing$.

proof.text:
Using the unique finite basis expansions of [def-weil-pbc-free-module], define
$$P_n\left(\sum_{v,I:\,|I|=n}m_{v,I}[v,I]\right)=\sum_{v,I:\,|I|=n}m_{v,I}p(v,I).$$
The sum is finite and unambiguous. Coefficientwise addition of expansions proves additivity. Every homomorphism having the prescribed generator values must have this value on each expansion, proving uniqueness. For $n<0$ or $n>r$, the source is zero and its unique homomorphism is zero. This constructs the unique degree-preserving family for every integer $n$.

proof.text: The same finite-expansion construction from [def-weil-pbc-free-module] defines $\tau_w$ on $C_a$ by the prescribed generator values; it preserves degree. For each $(a,b)$ the function $(x,y)\mapsto\tau_wx\otimes\tau_wy$ is bilinear, hence [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives the homomorphism $\tau_w\otimes\tau_w$ on that tensor summand. Sum it componentwise to obtain diagonal translation on $T_n$. On generators, $\tau_0=1$ and $\tau_w\tau_z=\tau_{w+z}$; finite expansions, bilinearity and finite-support sums give these identities on $C$ and $T$ as well. Thus these really are translation actions.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary open direct image, algebraic expansion below the tame-boundary route; the cubical formula and the following calculations are agent-written, not asserted by that paragraph.

proof.text:
For each generator, applying the diagonal translation of step 5 to the formula of steps 3 and 4 gives
$$(\tau_w\otimes\tau_w)P_{|I|}[v,I]=\sum_{A\sqcup B=I}\epsilon(A,B)[v+w,A]\otimes[v+u_A+w,B]=P_{|I|}[v+w,I].$$
The last equality uses $v+u_A+w=v+w+u_A$ in $\mathbf Z^r$; the partitions and their signs do not depend on $v$. By the unique finite expansions of [def-weil-pbc-free-module], equality on these generators gives $P_n\tau_w=(\tau_w\otimes\tau_w)P_n$ on all of $C_n$. For a zero source both sides are zero. This proves precisely the required graded equivariance.
